launches.tagline: An agent that is triggered by alerts and surfaces relevant information that helps you troubleshoot
launches.body:
⭐ Star us on [Github](https://github.com/vespperhq/vespper) & follow us on [Twitter](https://x.com/vespperdotcom) & [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/vespper)!

**📜 TL;DR**

[Vespper](https://www.vespper.com?utm_source=yc&utm_campaign=yclaunch&utm_id=1) is an on-call engineer that helps engineers troubleshoot alerts by surfacing the right data at the right time.\
\
<https://youtu.be/uN888sOaIig>

**🎯 What is Vespper?**

Vespper is an on-call engineer running 24/7 to troubleshoot your alerts and surface the right data to help you resolve your issue so incidents never falls through the cracks.

Whether your company is going through growing pains, needs a better handle at dealing with SEV0 or has too many low priority unsolved issues - Vespper will adapt to your needs to democratize expert knowledge across your organization.

**❌ The problem**

Most companies drown in alerts and there are too many alerts to handle.

* **Engineers** hate waking up at 3am to go investigate an issue, one person is familiar with one specific thing and they aren’t around, there is a constant need to check for false positives.
* **Product managers** are left playing hot potato when trying to figure out the impact of incidents and bugs but engineers are too busy triaging the issue itself.
* **Customer support** are left asking “who owns” which service when triaging tickets.
* **Engineering leaders** need to constantly ensure engineers are escalating quickly, they rely on service specialists to debug an issue other engineers aren’t familiar with but they aren’t always around during critical times.

**💰 The solution**

Vespper is a multi-agent system that triages alerts, troubleshoots them and sends findings in seconds to Slack. It’s connected to internal tools (observability, incident management, knowledge management, codebases and more) and can surface problems & identify patterns in the oceans of data you have.

At the moment, we support popular tools such as:

* **Observability** - DataDog, Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, SigNoz, Coralogix
* **Incident management** - PagerDuty, Opsgenie
* **Codebases** - Github
* **Knowledge management** - Notion, Confluence, Jira
* **Communication** -  Slack, Teams (TBD)

**⚒️ How does it work?**

Vespper is a system that’s comprised of multi-agents and AIOps models. Behind the scenes, we run & coordinate multiple agents and tools that help identify suspicious patterns from your environment.

Using Vespper is easy.

1. Signup & create an organisation.
2. Connect the tools you work with when triaging/troubleshooting. This means observability, knowledge, incident management and communication tools.

Once the integrations are connected, we automatically trigger advanced data ingestion pipelines that starts scraping data from your environment. This is used to train the bot. You can see the status of the ingestion & training in our web UI.

Once the system is ready, it will start triaging alerts for you, post an hypothesis on Slack and show you all the automatic checks it made!

**👨‍👨‍👦 About the team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=85173&key=user_uploads/316431/58991bfd-e2eb-49f3-a915-31300d54e458)

Hi, we are Topaz & Dudu 😊 We co-founded Vespper with the mission of making on-call stress-free. \
\
**Topaz (CEO)** - Spent years at Snyk (a hyper-growth unicorn) building and maintaining large distributed systems, leading PLG experiments and achieving 99.9% uptime for her teams services.

**Dudu (CTO)** - has seven years of experience working at rapidly-growing technology startups, including Google, Viz.ai and SafeBreach. Dudu was a deep-learning algorithm engineer at Viz.ai. He contributed to cutting-edge projects that leverage computer vision for healthcare applications and also worked on large-scale distributed systems.

We both dealt with daily alerts and the daily monotony of triaging, tuning and maintaining services observability.  This time spent all came at the expense of working on more impactful customer focused work.

We believe that pairing the strength of AI to pattern-match, classic AIOps and heuristics from our own experience can unlock a new experience for developers.

**🙏 Our ask**

1. Book a meeting with us <https://cal.com/callwithtopaz/vespper> or email us at [**founders@vespper.com**](mailto:founders@vespper.com)**.**
2. Star us on [GitHub](https://github.com/vespperhq/vespper) + follow along on [Twitter](https://x.com/vespperdotcom) & [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/101636115/).

launches.tagline: Vetnio records patient consultations, automating note-taking and other administrative work, so veterinarians can focus more on patient care.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:**

* ⏰ Veterinarians spend \~40% of their time on admin work, with note-taking alone making up \~20% of their time.
* 🎤 By recording patient meetings, Vetnio automatically generates clinical notes and emails in seconds.
* ✨ Additionally, Vetnio helps out with diagnostics, follow-ups, invoice generation, and more, reducing the risk of missed revenue for clinics while ensuring optimal care for animals.

[Introducing Vetnio](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z6KIg5SJUUk)

# **Who are we and why are we doing this?**

We are [Arman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/armankaregar/) and [Max](https://www.linkedin.com/in/max-henry-xie/) from [Vetnio](https://vetnio.com). Being close friends for +10 years, Vetnio is the second startup we have co-founded together. We both have exceptional backgrounds within engineering, with Arman having 20 years of audio processing experience and Max being a self-taught developer since childhood.

It all started when Arman brought his 🐶, Knut  (picture below), to a stressful veterinary visit. He noticed how much time was spent by the veterinarian typing on a keyboard and immediately went on to think how this can be made better. After a quick discussion with Max, the idea for Vetnio was born.

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcJzgeyF-gX-baUP0NVgep-EMa_iTLVKHwA9rQoA-Z6QiaTH4EpLeBazL_R_eKkrjHpWEyoNOZB-jKapY7RZ8S4hJesNc3OloZI59SRuyT8aI3ffpGw4lX3YGGRBEbn5k9hIoqThw?key=3XWI3B5KbKFPqOSqe7jrNCyD)

**Problem**\
With a rising patient load, veterinarians are overworked and stressed, leading to mistakes, burnout, and lost revenue. Admin work takes up \~40% of their time, and that's where Vetnio comes in.

**Solution**\
Vetnio has built an AI Copilot that records meetings and writes clinical notes, thereby saving veterinarians and clinics time, money, and headaches. Additionally, Vetnio helps out with diagnostics, follow-ups, invoice generation, and more, reducing the risk of missed revenue for clinics while ensuring optimal care for animals.

[Demo video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PeoKr2yXSw)

**Case studies and traction**\
Among others, we work closely with the global leader in veterinary care, IVC Evidensia, and are currently conducting pilots with several prominent veterinary chains. Recently, the largest veterinary magazine in the Nordics published an independent interview with Evidensia, highlighting how our solution was saving them up to [15 minutes per 45-minute consultation](https://www.svenskveterinartidning.se/effektivare-journalforing-med-ai/), significantly reducing their administrative workload.

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfl83aqSvXXbGlasaxpV0KXvgWps3LVxtVBnZiqCJviBcFmdyDyYwQbF6sug1O5t5dOBdLIJZ4jQvmLabMYOKqHTe00w-7iq77XJK00_KgfygNsDw5RCTP0Z6IwtdUB4wTfGfZX?key=3XWI3B5KbKFPqOSqe7jrNCyD)

📸: A veterinarian at Evidensia is reading through the text on Vetnio after a consultation.

Rest of the engineers:

* Emil Franzell
* Arvid Norström
* Rakin Ali
* Marcel Laska

Other notable team members include:

Microsoft Word serves over a billion users, but Copilot is still stuck in the Stone Age, requiring manual selection just to generate crude, format-ignoring block replacement edits completely devoid of context from your preferences, files, or the web.

With a single prompt, Praxim makes edits across your entire document:

Praxim knows exactly what to change and what to keep and edits with word-level granularity—precisely editing only what needs editing, not making brute block replacements.

* Actual lists, tables, and styles—not fake imitation structures that are actually just paragraphs

Pull data, research, and edit all without leaving Word, with features that 10x your productivity:

Praxim is already used for use cases from form filling with data from multiple sources to contract redlining with precise legal edits.

**Why only now?** Programmers left the era crude AI assistance years ago with agentic code editors. Formatted document editing is a far harder technical problem—a single word is encoded by formatting and structural markup several orders of magnitude more complex than plaintext code, with countless ways to render correct text incorrectly. Semantic meaning and formatting both matter.

Praxim for Word solves this, delivering a quantum leap over any other Word editing tool today. Start using Praxim today at [praxim.ai](http://praxim.ai)!

Hey everyone! We just launched our Mac app designed to make every meeting as natural as it would be in your native language.  The app transcribes and translates all audio you hear, and allows you to decide when to translate your voice as speech into the meeting.

It's invisible to others (like Granola), and works everywhere without any meeting bots. Try it at [**startpinch.com**](http://startpinch.com)!

Here’s a live demo, without cuts: \
[**https://youtu.be/ltM2p-SosLc**](https://youtu.be/ltM2p-SosLc)

**Our story**

When we first launched Pinch, we shipped a video conferencing solution with a human-like AI interpreter that was an active participant in your call. Our users hold the spacebar down while speaking to the translator, and when they release the spacebar the translator speaks out to the entire room.

That design was intentional - it puts the task of context selection on the user and prevents people from interrupting each other (only one person can press spacebar at a time).  It also comes with heavy tradeoffs, such as longer meeting lengths and friction with first-time users.

**Why we're excited about the desktop app:**

1. No vendor lock-in, invisible to others, and works everywhere - just select Pinch Microphone.
2. Fast transcription+translation means you can understand what's going on in real-time and interrupt where necessary.
3. After you start speaking, the others will hear your translated audio as fast as we can generate it, without interrupting your flow.

The last few months, our focus has been on building a translation model and UX that would support fast and accurate cross-lingual meetings, and we’re incredibly excited to open the public beta today.

Join the MacOS beta at [**startpinch.com**](http://startpinch.com)

launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re Christian and Keyu — co-founders of [Pinch](https://startpinch.com).\
\
**TL;DR**\
Pinch is an online meeting platform that enables immersive international video calls. Our platform translates your voice in real-time so you can speak and understand over 30 languages. Watch our demo [here](https://youtu.be/Cu7KlbZ3gjw), or try it for free on our [website](https://startpinch.com).

**The problem**\
We’ve felt first-hand how language barriers can actively limit a team’s productivity. High bandwidth communication is vital for collaboration, and while we’ve all moved from IRC → VoIP → Video Conferencing, the existing translation tools still operate in low-bandwidth mediums (mostly caption transcriptions). This makes conversations difficult because 1) converting audio to text before translation is slower, 2) you lose all information of how something was said, and 3) you’re no longer having a face-to-face meeting.\
\
**Our solution**\
We knew there had to be a better way to connect across different languages and cultures, so we started building Pinch. Shortly after, we found out how challenging translation truly was.  Balancing latency/accuracy for chunk-based audio translation, capturing inflection and tonality per statement, handling culturally specific phrasing, and making a seamless meeting experience are all unsolved problems we're taking on. \
\
We’re currently in public beta with our own meeting platform, supporting live use-cases in personal connections (e.g. meeting in-laws for the first time), as well as business (foreign clients, international sales, inter-team comms.).\
\
👥 **Our team**\
[Christian](https://linkedin.com/in/christiansafka) — 10 years of experience launching software and AI-native products 0→1, ex-TPM at Microsoft and most recently the Head of ML at Tavus (YC S21).\

Hey! We’re Kevin and Regina from [Dexterity](https://getdexterity.com/). Today, we’re launching Dex—the fastest interface for co-working with AI, right inside your browser.

**TLDR:** **AI that works _with you,_ not just for you**. 10x your workflows without breaking your flow. Try [**Dex**](https://youtu.be/H6hMAVkGp8M) (Beta) → [**getdexterity.com**](http://getdexterity.com)

### **Why We’re Building This**

**Four weeks before Demo Day, we pivoted to build for ourselves.**

Most AI web agents today are “set-and-forget” chats—you hand them off and check back later. But what about workflows you actually _want_ to drive? Navigating platforms, moving data, making quick decisions—these moments demand instant, context-aware models that work with you, not just for you.

Imagine using Operator to order DoorDash—a frustratingly back-and-forth relay with no real-time visibility. That same friction exists for work tools like Jira, GSuite, and GitHub, where users need instant feedback and responsive action, not slow AI handoffs.

**That’s why we’re taking a Cursor (vs. Devin) approach—for the browser.**

### **The Problem**

Modern work is a juggling act of 15+ tabs, software bloat, and constant UI friction, just to complete a single task.

The real bottleneck isn’t just automation—it’s context switching. Traditional solutions force users to memorize shortcuts (appeals to devs, but leaves everyone else behind), while AI tools make you adapt to them instead of living right where you work.

**Why not turn your browser itself into an intelligent personal workspace?**

### **How It Works**

With simple voice and text, Dex enhances familiar interfaces, automates mundane actions, and understands your intent.

* **Smart Navigation**🔸Find, execute, and move between apps.
* **Suggest Context**🔸Cut down tab-switching and manual searching.
* **Cross-App Automation**🔸Shortcut multi-step workflows, zero setup.
* **Adaptive UI/UX**🔸Reshape, replicate, and browse by your rules.

Think of it like Spotlight Search meets AI automation + personal expert for everyday apps.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=87902&key=user_uploads/1003357/5841f4c8-281d-4bdd-a4b0-053d44c7b41d)

### **Use Cases**

* **GSuite** – Write emails, find docs, and move data anywhere.
* **GitHub** – Search repos, manage issues, and navigate faster.
* **Omni AI** – Talk to and reference live tabs or integrated apps.

### **Coming Soon…**

* **Meetings** 📅 → Create and join calendar and Zoom events instantly
* **Sales** 💼 → Automate clicks across LinkedIn, Sheets, and Apollo.io
* **Snippets** ✂️ → Dex captures notes, links, and frequent snippets
* **Food** 🍔 → Speak to browse options and order DoorDash

### **Our Ask**

We’re building Dex for power users, founders, students, and curious explorers—because that’s who we are.

[**Join our waitlist**](https://getdexterity.com/) → **Get notified when Dex goes live on the Chrome store**.\
[**Follow us on Twitter**](https://x.com/dexterity_ai) → Stay updated on latest features.\
[**Discord**](https://x.com/dexterity_ai) → Get to know us more personally + brainstorm cool ideas.

Drop dream features to [regina@getdexterity.com](mailto:regina@getdexterity.com) and let us know what you think!

**TL;DR:** Zero is an open source AI-native email client that organizes your inbox, summarizes threads, writes replies, and lets you chat with your email, so you can stay effortlessly on top of work.

**What is Zero and how does it work?**

Zero makes email work for you, not the other way around (checkout our launch video below!).

[Launch Video](https://youtu.be/3Hy3jEQQVFQ)

Zero uses AI to:

* **Prioritize** emails and surface what matters most
* **Summarize** long email threads into quick takeaways
* **Draft** and **Reply** to emails automatically
* **Organize** your inbox into smart categories, let you chat with your inbox, understand projects, and plan your day.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=90228&key=user_uploads/2556219/4f2601b3-7b85-4447-8b75-9f78c3d6c314)

Traditional email clients are outdated and passive. They overload you with notifications, bury important messages, and force you to manually manage threads, tasks, and follow-ups. Meanwhile, most “AI” email tools are just bolt-on features, slow, clunky, and unaware of the full context of your inbox.

**Our Solution**\
Zero is built from the ground up as an **AI-native email platform**. That means every part of your experience, from prioritization to replies, is powered by a deep understanding of your inbox and your workflow. Zero doesn’t just help you **handle** email, it helps you get **ahead** of it.

* AI that thinks like a human assistant, not a search algorithm
* Real-time summaries and smart organization that adapts to your day
* A seamless way to interact with your email through natural conversation
* Fully open source for complete transparency

**Try Zero**

Instead of drowning in an endless stream of emails, Zero gives you a live, intelligent inbox you can actually control.

launches.body:
Hey everyone we’re Harsha and Dhruv from Slashy. Our goal is to define the next generation of email, by building an email platform that actually works for you, and learns over time. \
\
**TLDR:** Slashy is the next big email platform after Superhuman, the first with an assistant built in. Slashy can do everything from writing drafts in your tone, texting you when an important email comes in, prepping you for calls, to the things you expect from a true email client like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, a mobile app and more. All while continuously learning about you and your preferences, so it only gets better over time. The average user takes 5 minutes to get set up and saves an extra hour a day. Read an independent review from Tom’s guide (1m+ subscribers) [here](https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/slashy-is-the-ai-email-app-replacing-notion-mail-heres-why).

You can get started for free at [slashy.com](http://slashy.com), and use our YC deal for a long-term discount.

**Launch Video:** <https://youtu.be/o2TN-wwCYm8>

## **Problem**

Most founders we speak to, have one of two problems (sometimes both)

1. They spend too much time manually handling email, and not enough building their company.
2. They don’t spend enough time on email, and lose important deals/hires due to things slipping.

## **Solution**

That’s why we built Slashy, the first email platform that reliably gets work done for you, whether it be drafting emails, notifying you when a prospect replies, schedule meetings, or more. Slashy works wherever you work best, so onboarding is seamless (just ask some of our users). It takes 10 minutes to set up, and saves the average email power user an extra one hour a day. It does this by:

1. **Doing all the basic things right:** Stuff like keyboard shortcuts, open tracking, unified inbox, team comments, availability links, all come part of Slashy. So you don’t lose anything transitioning from Gmail, Superhuman, Front and more. ([@Jayme Hoffman](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/60463) actually switched to Slashy being surprised just that a new email client could match the speed, shortcuts of something like Superhuman)
2. **Writing drafts that sound like you:** Claude drafts sound like slop because they just look at the thread. Slashy does a lot more, it looks at the linkedin/web of recipients, past emails you’ve sent, past changes you’ve made to prior drafts, and more including using our own custom-built memory system for email. (Fun fact we have a special tool for handling suggesting times/scheduling as base llms are very bad at this). ([@Michelle Marcelline](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/379052) pretty much just hits send on all her Slashy drafts with minimal edits)
3. **A powerful sidebar:** Slashy comes with a cursor-like sidebar. That lets you do things like search, draft, schedule and more. So you no longer need to keep flipping between ChatGPT and your email. ([@Yahia Bakour](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2538368) loves this to power thorugh drafts and replies)
4. **Integrations:** Slashy connects to not just your email, but your meeting notes (Granola, Fathom, Circleback, etc.), crm (Attio, Hubspot, Salesforce, etc.), Notion and more since the context to handle email isn’t just in email. ([@Pavlos Markesinis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2511438) loves how Slashy connects to his Attio and makes life simple)
5. **Automations:** The best assistants also know when to handle things in the background. So Slashy can also automatically do things like prep you for calls, text you when an important email comes in, and more. ([@Owen Botkin](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2579867) relies on Slashy to prep him from calls, and [@Pranav Madhukar](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1531197) doesn’t even check his email anymore unless Slashy alerts him an email comes in)
6. **iMessage/Slack Bot:** One of the worst parts of traditional clients? You need to open them to see if something important comes in. Slashy can ping you on text/slack so you don’t even need to context switch. (@devansh is one of our bigger Slack fans, while [@Abhinav Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/979064) for iMessage).
7. **Voice:** Sometimes it’s easier to speak your mind than write (or you’re driving and just can’t haha). So Slashy lets you dictate your thoughts, and our AI will make it sound like a much better version of you. Or you can talk with our voice to voice agent when you’re commuting (@vishruth is one of our power users for our voice drafts).
8. **Personalized Memory:** Slashy gets better the more you use it. It keeps notes on how you write, who you talk to, when you schedule, and also it learns from every edit you made before hitting send. It even once a week goes back and rewrites its notes to better match you. After all you'd expect a human assistant to be smarter after a few months, why not your ai one. ([@Devraj Gopal](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2057015) loves how Slashy has grown to know him more and more).
9. **Natural Language Labels:** A common complaint we hear is the rise of the AI SDR, and how everyone’s inbox is inundated with emails. The problem with traditional labelling systems is they don’t adjust over time, leading to important emails getting missed. Slashy’s labelling system does, leading to a much better filtering rate, and fewer dropped balls. ([@Nazli Danis](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/520906) was drowning in spam before Slashy)

## Security and Privacy

We take security/privacy as an email client very seriously.  We’ve already gotten CASA, and SOC II. We also get monthly pen-tests done by [@Casco](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/30477) to ensure our users' data is safe. None of our AI providers train on your data as well.

## Getting Started

Now if you want to get started just go to[ slashy.com](http://slashy.com), or you can book a time here if you’d like me to demo the product/ask any questions just shoot an email to [founders+ea@slashy.com](mailto:founders+ea@slashy.com), and Slashy will schedule a time that works for both of us :)

**📙 TL;DR**

Trace is a workflow automation platform that routes tasks to the right agent – human or AI.

By connecting to tools like Slack, Jira, and Notion, Trace breaks down existing workflows, spots automation opportunities, and embeds AI agents to handle repetitive tasks – without disrupting how your team works. More than 30 companies already use Trace to automate gruntwork.

**Ask**: If you’re currently working in operations, product, or support teams, we’d love to talk. Email us at [founders@trace.so](mailto:founders@trace.so) ‼️

**❌ The Problem**

Most teams lose ≈ 40% of their productivity on repetitive manual tasks. 

Routine work like chasing updates, filling docs, coordinating teams, and handling support drains hours, breaks focus, and slows execution.

Meanwhile, employees aren’t sure which tasks can be automated, which agents to use, or which tools to trust – problems made worse by fragmented data and lost context.

Even worse, most AI tools work alone, disconnected from both teams and the people using them.

✅ **Our Solution** 

Trace is an AI-native workspace that breaks down existing workflows, assigns repetitive tasks to AI agents, and routes the rest to the right people.

With Trace, AI works across your entire team – passing tasks between agents and people without disrupting operations.

It respects permissions, learns from past and ongoing work, tracks progress with a full audit trail, and lets you review, edit, or reroute tasks in a simple interface.

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=91579&key=user_uploads/978619/4443ca80-d250-46a5-8234-98a9d5852a59)

Hey 👋, we’re Haz and Wyatt, the founders of Pally.

We’re building Pally because in a world full of ‘AI SDRs’, our warm connections become more important than ever… Yet today, keeping track of thousands of connections across countless social platforms is impossible. 

We forget to respond, we miss important moments, and we lose touch.

We’re building Pally to solve that.

If this resonates, we’d love your early feedback. Download Pally here: [www.pally.com](http://www.pally.com)

# Demo

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g97sd_roD14

## How does it work?

We bring together all your connections, across all your socials (inc. iMessage, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Google, Email, Calendar, and X), and then our AI researches everything they’ve ever posted online.

Pally uses this deep understanding of each relationship to help you:

* Prepare you for meetings
* Stay in touch with your potential customers/hires/investors (or just remind you to ring your mum from time to time)
* Search over your network to find the right person for any query (”who do I know in New York that I’ve not spoken to in a while?”)
* Add people to pipelines

We also added some fun relationship stats, so you can see how social you are compared to other Pally users, how each relationship is growing/declining over time, how long you take to reply vs how long others take to reply to you, and more.

## Who’s it for?

We’re mostly focused on founders and investors, but we’ve also seen salespeople, recruiters, agency owners, and creators get a lot of value from Pally; essentially anyone in a role where relationships are a primary focus (and honestly, we believe in the world of AI, that’s _everyone_).

## What's next?

We're excited to launch this into public beta today, learn from what our users are loving, and where they’re wanting more, and build that. 

Our roadmap includes adding integrations with AI meeting note takers, so all your relationship context is in one place, adding an iOS app so you have all your data on the go, and adding more agentic capabilities.

# Ask

Please upvote us here and on [Product Hunt](https://www.producthunt.com/products/pally-ai-relationship-management), and give Pally a test and let us know how you get on! 

We’re also hiring! If you’re interested in working with us, please email [hiring@pally.com](mailto:hiring@pally.com) with your cv.

Thanks for your support,

Haz + Wyatt 🫶

launches.body:
Hi everyone,

We’re [Sam](http://linkedin.com/in/samurdhilbk) and [Anushka](http://linkedin.com/in/anushkaidamekorala/), co-founders of [Logical](https://trylogical.ai).

**TL;DR:**

**Logical is a copilot that lives on your desktop and proactively assists with things like drafting emails, meeting insights and tracking to-do items.**

Instead of waiting for you to prompt, Logical suggests context-aware actions in many common apps and services. It’s like Clippy, but actually good.

https://youtu.be/XfyPZb14LZM?si=aaJMF37-ipwkJBDV

### Problem

Prompt-first AI is fundamentally flawed. We waste hours every week writing lengthy prompts, context-switching and copy-pasting to get a chatbot to understand what we're doing. The context surrounding our work (emails, meeting notes, knowledge bases etc.) lives in siloed services that don't talk to each other. A truly helpful AI must live where we work: on the desktop.

### Solution

Logical lives on your desktop, observing your work to build an understanding of your intent and the context that surrounds it. As you switch between apps and tabs, Logical transfers that context with you.

It proactively suggests actions based on what you're doing—whether you're in Gmail, Slack, or Excel. This turns Logical into an all-in-one assistant: it's your email drafter, to-do manager, AI note-taker, and chatbot, all combined.

launches.tagline: We cut your Claude Code costs by 47% in one line of install. Same models, same workflow, half the price.
launches.body:
**TLDR**: **Tokenmaxxing is out. Tokenminning is in.** Quotient Labs sits on top of Claude Code and reduces the amount of context you pay for—without changing your models, prompts, projects, or workflow. Across real, multi-step developer workflows, we’ve benchmarked **47% lower token cost with no measured quality loss.** Get started today at <https://www.quotientlabs.com/>.

**The Problem**

Coding agents accumulate a lot of context.

Every file read, search result, test run, tool output, generated plan, and conversation turn gets added to the session. As the session grows, this history is repeatedly re-read (and re-billed) long after it has stopped being useful in its original form. The result? **You’re overpaying Claude for tokens your agent never needed.**

**Fermat’s Last Token** (our main product) sits on top of Claude Code and optimizes what enters and remains in your model’s context. We do this in four ways:

1. **Faster, more cost-efficient agent tools** that batch operations and return compact, information-dense results.
2. **Bash output compression** that preserves the useless parts of long command and test outputs while removing the bloat.
3. **Live text compression** that removes the information-sparse and irrelevant tokens in conversation turns before they ever compound in cost. 
4. **Idle context optimization** that compresses older conversation history as the prompt cache expires (this is more often than you think; only 5 minutes TTL) while preserving the freshest context verbatim.

The important part: **you keep using Claude Code exactly as you do today.**

**Observability**: See real-time estimated cost and savings down to the session and request level, as well as manage your organizations and users, in the user dashboard: <https://console.quotientlabs.com/>. 

**Ready to go in 30 seconds.** Install Fermat, sign in, and continue using Claude Code normally:

**curl -fsSL [https://downloads.quotientlabs.com/fermat/install.sh](https://downloads.quotientlabs.com/fermat/install.sh) | bash && fermat login**

**Fermat is compatible with both CLI and the VS Code extension.** Your existing projects, prompts, models, integrations, and interface are untouched.

You can bypass Fermat (if you really want) on a particular chat any time with _claude --vanilla._ You can also fully uninstall in one line with _fermat uninstall_ (though we don’t recommend either :)).

**Our ask**

We’re looking for devs and engineering teams who use Claude Code heavily, especially on long-running, tool-intensive engineering tasks. 

We’d love to get feedback on where Fermat helps the most, where compression could be better, and any features or changes you’d like to see.

**TLDR:** Cofia learns how you work and proactively automates your repetitive tasks. No more prompting or workflow builders.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6pgSb0ZxMhI>

🧑🏻‍💻👩🏻‍💻 **Founders**

We're Pao and Moses. We've spent years in high-growth tech companies -- Pao running retention at Brilliant, Moses leading monetization at Duolingo.

❌ **The problem**

We kept seeing the same pattern: smart people are still doing manual tasks.

Everyone talks about AI saving time, but the reality? Most AI tools require you to:

* Recognize the opportunities for automation
* Describe your exact workflow in a prompt
* Learn new interfaces and configure new tools

So despite having "AI assistants," people are still spending hours on repetitive work that could be automated… if only custom AI tools could build themselves.

✅ **The solution:**

Traditional AI waits for you to describe what you need. Cofia proactively builds personalized automations, trained on _your_ exact workflows, by securely processing the work you actually do.

No prompts. No remembering to turn it on. No describing what you do.

How it works:

* Cofia learns about the specific repetitive tasks you do
* When it recognizes a pattern, it builds a custom agent and then offers it to you
* You review, launch it, and never do that task manually again

Sample tasks we’ll detect:

* Building prospect lists
* Outreach, follow-ups, scheduling
* Maintaining recruiting pipelines
* Creating data reports

❓**Is this magic?**

We hope it feels that way! Under the hood, we’re listening to system events and anonymized network traffic. This gets mined for repeatable patterns of activity, which serves as the framework for the automations we spin up. No need to screen record like traditional RPA task mining, and you can see what we’re processing at any time.

launches.tagline: Run multiple coding agents in parallel.
launches.body:
Hey YC! 👋 We’re Arne and Raban the we’re building [Emdash](https://emdash.sh). An [open-source](http://github.com/generalaction/emdash) desktop app that lets you work with multiple coding agents at once. We’re calling it an Agentic Development Environment (ADE).

<https://youtu.be/jdIPf2cxf6w>

💬 **Problem**\
Every time we used a coding agent, we'd start a task and ... wait. We tried running multiple agents on the same repo and ended up with branch chaos and merge conflicts. When a new model dropped – Opus, Codex, Gemini flash, Kimi, whatever – we had no clean way to test it against our current setup on the same task. We were bouncing between terminals, GitHub, and our IDE.\
\
⏩ **Solution**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97799&key=user_uploads/1755188/dd08968b-2b60-4a85-b998-e8cc9d017dfc)

Emdash is an environment for agentic development that lets you run multiple agents side-by-side safely, review what each one did in one place, and create a PR when it looks right.

🔍 **How it works**

* Start a task → Emdash spins up a new git worktree so nothing touches your main directory
* Choose any agent, out of 20+ providers(incl. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini)
* Run multiple agents at once without conflicts
* Compare diffs, make quick manual edits if needed, and create a PR

🧰 **What’s included**

* Worktree isolation per agent
* Issue handoff from Linear / Jira / GitHub
* One place to review diffs and ship PRs
* Lifecycle scripts + CI/CD hooks
* Best-of-N comparisons
* Integrated file editor + browser preview
* Remote project access via SSH

We natively embed \~20 agent providers (including Claude Code, Codex, Continue, and Codebuff), so you can use the latest models inside the same workflow.

To get started run `brew install –cask emdash`or download directly from[ GitHub releases](https://github.com/generalaction/emdash/releases). We’re available on macOS and Linux.

**🙏 Our Asks**

1. Try [Emdash](https://emdash.sh/) - it’s free and open-source
2. Give us a star on [GitHub](http://github.com/generalaction/emdash) **🌟**

Questions or feedback? Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/m9APwzK4qd) or email us at [founders@emdash.sh](mailto:founders@emdash.sh)

— Arne & Raban

**TL;DR:** Robby is a growth platform that converts every technician visit into revenue. We combine third-party and customer data to uncover high-intent leads and prepare technicians with talking points that increase sales rates. Early customers are seeing 6 figures in opportunities every week with Robby.

**Ask:** If you know any owners or GMs at home services businesses, please introduce us! [founders@tryrobby.com](mailto:founders@tryrobby.com)

**Problem**

Home services businesses generate enormous amounts of valuable data every day, but most of it never turns into revenue. Technicians are in customers’ homes constantly, observing aging equipment, safety issues, and upgrade needs. (For example, they might be called to service a furnace and won’t notice the 20 year old boiler next to it.) That information is often: 

* Captured inconsistently (or not at all)
* Hard to operationalize across a team
* Invisible to owners and GMs until it’s too late

The result: high-intent opportunities are missed, close rates vary wildly by technician, and leadership lacks a real-time view of revenue potential, **even while demand is already there**.

**Solution**

Robby turns every technician visit into a structured growth opportunity: 

* Ingests customer, technician, and third-party data
* Uses AI to surface dozens of high-intent opportunities each day
* Equips technicians clear, contextual talking points to guide customer conversations
* Capture customer insights that would otherwise be lost through lightweight voice AI
* Provides GMs a single command center to monitor pipeline and drive revenue

 

All without changing how technicians or office teams already work. Today, we have several paying customers who are each uncovering 6 figures in additional revenue opportunities every week. On our first day of launch, Robby helped close **$40k in new business within the first hour.**

**Product Launch**

<https://youtu.be/zOBrEP3oyfk>

**Product Demo**

<https://www.tella.tv/video/30s-robby-opportunity-dashboard-55xb>

**Why we’re building Robby** 

Before building Robby, we spent months embedded in the home services industry. We rode along with dozens of HVAC technicians and shadowed dispatch, CSRs, sales managers, and GMs. We focused on understanding where data breaks down in day-to-day operations, and where real leverage actually exists. 

We’re currently studying for the EPA 608 certification so we can become certified technicians ourselves. We believe the best vertical software starts with deep respect for the work and the people doing it.

Our team brings experience building and scaling products at Ironclad, Porter, Affinity, Uber, and Cloud Health Systems, and advising growth and software acquisitions for PE firms at Bain. We met at Harvard Business School and dropped out to work on Robby full-time.

**TL;DR: Marker partners with execs, learns how their organization actually works, finds the highest-impact problems, and solves them by** **shipping custom AI agents into production on the Marker platform in weeks. Each agent deepens our understanding of the business, so the next agent launches faster. We stay embedded until the business is rebuilt.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O829Y4wlKvk>

We’re Will Drevno, Richard Berwick, and David Pastewka, the founders of Marker. We’ve built together for 15 years. Our last company, Drapr (YC S20), was acquired by Gap Inc., and Richard went on to found Gap’s Office of AI.

## **Why we built Marker**

Inside Gap, we saw firsthand how much leaders wanted to transform their businesses with AI and how hard it was to turn that ambition into production systems that actually changed how their organizations worked.

**95% of AI initiatives still fail. Ours don’t.**

The hard part is understanding how work happens across people, systems, and teams; choosing the opportunities that matter most; and getting solutions into production.

## **How Marker works**

We embed with each company and lead the transformation end to end:

* **Understand the organization.** We listen closely to leaders and frontline teams, learn their systems and ways of working, and map the processes that usually live in people’s heads.
* **Find the biggest opportunities.** We identify and prioritize the problems where AI can have the greatest impact on cost, capacity, speed, or growth.
* **Build and ship.** We create custom agents and automations around the company’s real workflows and systems. The agents we deploy run on the Marker Command Center and go live in production within weeks.
* **Compound.** Every agent we deploy deepens our understanding of the company. That helps us launch the next one faster and makes Marker increasingly integral to how the organization operates.

## **Who we’re working with today**

We’re rebuilding companies from mid-size through Fortune 500.

## **Why us**

We’ve sat on every side of this: founders selling into enterprises, operators transforming one from the inside, and executives responsible for enterprise AI. Marker is the company we wish we could have hired at Gap.

## **Our ask**

**If you are (or you know) a leader looking for real AI transformation—not another pilot, deck, or self-serve tool—please send them our way.**

**the problem**\
The bottleneck in development keeps moving. It used to be writing the code. Then agents solved that, and it became reviewing the code. Now what's left is planning the next step, and every IDE still waits.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102348&key=user_uploads/3131989/cb840d79-95f8-446d-b4cd-a60e9db72a85)

**the solution** \
Ara closes the loop. It proactively plans your next step, handing you proposals you can discard or send off to follow up on, with self-improving memory across all your tools and sessions, and full visibility across chats, files, browsers, terminals, and review panes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102348&key=user_uploads/3131989/fc09658e-c84b-4e56-8b00-4485c3de72ae)

\
**team**\
Adi and Sven both studied EECS at UC Berkeley. Adi worked in applied ML, at Scale AI and previously built an IDE company. Sven was an ML engineer on production systems and chaired Norway's largest student AI org. Serial hackathon winners, they've built and lived together across four cities and dropped out to build the IDE they always wanted.

The goal is an IDE that runs the development loop end to end, not one that waits for instructions.

\
_The IDE for token-maxxers._

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102348&key=user_uploads/3131989/eb3b255b-1cc1-4f77-a1c5-aa2f22227b7b)

Try it! [**Download Ara**](https://ara.so/) and email us at [founders@ara.so](mailto:founders@ara.so) with your feedback.

name: Tasklet
long_description:
AI chatbots can answer questions, but they can't do your work — they aren't connected to your tools, can't take actions, and stop running when you close the tab. Meanwhile, knowledge workers are still spending most of their day switching between dozens of SaaS apps, manually stitching together workflows that should be automated.

Tasklet is the AI agent that actually does the work. It connects to every tool you use — via thousands of built-in integrations, any HTTP API, or MCP servers — and takes real actions on your behalf: pulling reports, updating CRMs, triaging emails, processing data, and more. When it needs a UI, it generates one on the fly. When it needs to crunch numbers or do bulk operations, it writes and runs code in a cloud sandbox. When it needs to interact with a website that doesn't have an API, it uses a real browser. And because it runs in the cloud 24/7, you can set up triggers to have it take ongoing responsibility for workflows — not just do something once, but handle it going forward.

The product is deliberately simple: a chat interface where you talk to an extremely capable agent. But underneath that simplicity is a cloud-native agent runtime, best-in-class context engineering, a universal connections layer, and multi-model support that keeps us on the frontier as AI improves. 

We think legacy SaaS is being unbundled by agents, and Tasklet is the operating system that ties it all together.
one_liner: Agents that own the work

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer: We met at Firebase and continued working together at Google after the acquisition. In 2020 we left to start a company together, initially building an email client called Shortwave. While adding an AI agent to Shortwave in late 2024, we noticed something surprising: some users kept asking for the agent and integrations without the email client. They wanted a general-purpose AI agent that could connect to all their work tools — not just email. So in 2025 we made a bold bet, building Tasklet as a standalone cloud AI agent for knowledge work.

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer:
We founded the company in 2020 as a team of ex-Firebase/Google engineers. We initially built Shortwave, an AI-powered email client. After ChatGPT launched, we went all-in on AI and built a conversational assistant for email that showed real traction.\
\
In fall 2024 we shipped a full AI agent inside Shortwave — and growth accelerated. We started adding integrations with CRMs, project management tools, and messaging apps, and were among the first products to support MCP. That's when something unexpected happened: users started telling us they wanted the agent and integrations but didn't care about the email client.

So in 2025 we made a bold move — we built Tasklet, a standalone cloud AI agent for knowledge work. We went from idea to first user in under 6 weeks, and it was a massive hit. Each new capability we shipped (v2 agent architecture, sandbox, computer use, triggers) accelerated growth further, and by January 2026 Tasklet alone was adding more monthly revenue than Shortwave had in its first 4 years.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
AI chatbots can answer questions, but they can't actually do your work. They aren't connected to your tools, they can't take actions, and they stop running the moment you close the tab. The result is that knowledge workers still spend most of their day switching between dozens of SaaS apps — pulling data from one, updating another, copy-pasting between tabs, and stitching together workflows manually.\
\
We're building the AI agent that replaces all of that: one app that connects to every tool you use, runs 24/7 in the cloud, can use a computer, and can take ongoing responsibility for entire workflows.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
In the long run, we believe most knowledge work will be done by AI agents, not humans. Tasklet is the operating system for that future — the place where you manage, direct, and collaborate with agents that handle your work across every tool.

If we truly succeed, the average knowledge worker will 10x their output not by working harder, but by delegating most of their routine work to agents that run 24/7. Legacy SaaS apps will fade into background infrastructure that agents access via API, and the human's job shifts from doing the work to directing it. We think this is as big a shift as the move from desktop software to cloud — and we're building the platform that makes it happen.

launches.body:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-sLwzskvqE>

When I was 18, I joined Magic, a frontier lab working on 100M token context coding models, as a reinforcement learning researcher.

While I worked there, I gradually grew more drawn to autonomous research. I truly felt that this could automate all the work I was doing at Magic, so in January, I left to start my own lab.

Introducing Aster — a major breakthrough for research.

Aster isn’t a single agent. It is the first autonomous lab orchestrating **thousands of research agents in parallel.**

We pointed Aster towards ProteinGym, a benchmark that measures how accurately models predict the effects of protein mutations. It set the world record in **30 minutes**.

And it did it efficiently:

    •    57x faster than single agent systems on the same task.

    •    One-third the cost for the same result.

But here’s what we realized: measurable problems are only a small sliver of research.

The hard ones were never measurable.

At Aster, we’re on a mission to automate open-ended research, research that defines its own problems before it can answer them.

The future doesn’t wait to be defined by benchmarks. Neither do we.

Read our research writeups at <https://asterlab.ai>.

launches.title: Pentagon - A coordination layer for humans and agents.
launches.tagline: A new kind of team: humans and agents, working together.
launches.body:
Hey YC! I'm [Edgar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edgarpavlovsky/), building [Pentagon](https://pentagon.run).

**TL;DR** Agents are everywhere but they don't have good ways to work together, so humans become the coordination bottleneck. Pentagon is a coordination layer where your agents communicate autonomously, coordinate on tasks, and get work done as a team.

**Book a demo and see it in action:** <https://pentagon.run>\
**Our launch video:** <https://youtu.be/D28Mi7AXAeY>

**Problem**

Agents are increasingly becoming AI teammates at work - coding, researching, ops, even talking to customers. But they work alone. Coordination is the bottleneck, and it shows up differently depending on where you sit:

* **Small teams** are spinning up agents from scratch and immediately hitting the ceiling: each one is powerful on its own, but getting them to actually work together means you're back in the loop, copy/pasting between terminals.
* **Enterprises** already have agents running everywhere across the org. The hard part is figuring out what they're doing, how they fit together, and how to keep track of it all.

Underneath both: humans are the middleware. Hours of human time burnt doing work meant for a mechanical turk. Today's tools weren't built for this - AI products are conversational and non-deterministic, and reproducing workflows is harder than ever.

**Org code**

There's a deeper layer to this. Great teams are built for the moment - the right team depends on the problem at hand, the resources you have, and even who's leading. This applies to agents the same as it does to humans: every problem has its own org structure.

Andrej Karpathy calls it "org code" - and points out that compared to classical orgs, agentic codes have powerful new properties: they’re reproducible and more transparent. We think that agents also allow organizations to be much more dynamic: they can adapt to problems in realtime, and open a new dimension of what it means to build a productive organization.

From [a popular Karpathy tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2031767720933634100):

![Image](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HIts8HMaIAAKjok?format=jpg&name=medium)

**Our first solution: Pentagon Studio**

Pentagon's mission is to build the coordination layer for humans and agents. We're starting with Pentagon Studio - a workspace designed to feel familiar to existing alternatives and shepherd companies into a new kind of collaborative work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101681&key=user_uploads/402484/286ecb28-a420-4390-81cf-f1c1b181ec5c)

In Pentagon Studio, you define your org structure and your agents run it. Agents live on a spatial canvas and pop up sticky notes with status updates - you see who's active, idle, or blocked at a glance. They message each other, delegate tasks, share context, and build self-evolving memory over time. As the human, your job is to design and manage the team; they do the coordination.

* **Spatial canvas.** Agents live on infinite canvases you can think of like an office. Zoom in on one agent's conversation, zoom out to see the whole operation. The "org IDE."
* **Autonomous coordination.** Realtime, event-driven communication between agents - no expensive polling loops. Agents take feedback from you, ping another agent to get work done, then ping you when they need you.
* **Agent persistence.** Agents maintain sessions indefinitely and compound institutional knowledge over time. Tribal knowledge for your agent team.
* **Shared skills & tools.** Manage capabilities at individual, team, workspace, or org level. Each agent inherits based on hierarchy.
* **Human multiplayer + human-in-the-loop.** In contrast to "zero-human company" angles, we see humans and agents collaborating across shared orgs. Your agents should be able to work with your coworkers' agents.

**Why now**

Agents are already inside companies. The infrastructure to coordinate them isn't. Every day this gap stays open, humans burn hours doing work meant for a mechanical turk and leaders lose transparency into how work actually gets done.

We believe the best version of the future is one where superintelligent agents are viewed as teammates and we work with them as partners. Every company already knows how to work with coworkers - agents fit into existing organizational frameworks better than we've been giving them credit for. They just need the infrastructure to coordinate.

**Ask**

If you're running agentic workflows in production and struggling to manage them, we’d love to chat. See Pentagon Studio in action and book a demo with us at <https://pentagon.run> or reach out to me personally, and let’s evolve your team: [edgar@pentagon.run](mailto:edgar@pentagon.run).

### TL;DR

**⚡ Hyper learns your entire company and puts it back into every AI you use. ⚡**

In just a few clicks, Hyper silently reads everything in your company, keeps it up-to-date and conflict-free in real-time, and then plugs back directly into the AI tools you already love. Hyper makes every AI workflow immediately smarter with zero effort.

### Asks

Tell us how you’re keeping your AIs on the same page as you. Markdown files in Git? GBrain? Manual pipelines? We’ll set you up on Hyper in <20 minutes and supercharge your company so you’ll never have to correct your agents again.

[Book a demo](https://heyhyper.cal.com/founders)\
[Interact with us on X](https://x.com/ycombinator/status/2053882832208929262?s=20)\
[Check us out on Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/y-combinator_hyper-is-building-the-self-driving-company-activity-7459648541150314496-6e5c)[ ](https://x.com/ycombinator/status/2053882832208929262?s=20)\
\
Launch video: <https://youtube.com/shorts/6XySjjG9KNA?si=zb2bP4_0sqMfYz62>

# Your AI doesn’t even know

You’re automating the boring work with agents so you can build more, faster. BUT:

* Agents forget your customers + your relationships
* Agents ignore know your taste, and code smelly, ugly features
* Agents can’t remember your pivots, and act on stale data
* Agents keep making the same mistakes over and over, no matter how many times you yell at them.

So you’ve tried some insane manual hacks:

* You paste dumps of the same context into every new chat.
* You write obvious skills for something that it should just "know".
* You commit markdown files in your codebase so everyone's AI is on the same page.
* You hack an off-the-shelf memory libraries to fit your unique story

…before you know it, you have a huge mess of broken agents, and no amount of pasting, screenshotting, or committing gives your AI the complete, living picture of your company.

# ENTER: HYPER

**Hyper fixes all of this without you having to do anything.**

1. Hyper quietly pulls out important info from every document, calendar invite, email, Slack, GitHub pull request, conversation, and more.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/2474cd22-beeb-4525-bc19-bd546bd3a91e)

2. As you work, Hyper’s agents combine, synthesize, clean up, and deduplicate all of it into an up-to-date perfect picture of your company.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/d727c84a-929b-44a9-b1de-283717b3f134)

3. Hyper quietly plugs into every AI tool you use and system you build, silently feeding back useful information without any ugly tool calls, interface spam, or distractions.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/e019494b-f3a9-4d81-8ff9-14b16168aa63)


Now your AI knows: _Who did we talk to last week? What customer is facing this bug? How much revenue do we need before next week’s meeting?_

But it also knows: _What’s our design philosophy? What sales strategy seems to work best with mid-level execs? What feedback isn’t worth paying attention to right now?_

Hyper builds this brain across your whole company — so the next time your agents get to work, they _just know_. And the next time your teammates sit down to work, _they just know too._

# A Bit About Us

**Kanyes** helped secure multi-million dollar deals at Snorkel AI and wrote motion algorithms at Matic Robots. He ran a streetwear arbitrage operation out of his sophomore year apartment. **Shalin** was one of Matic’s most prolific designers and engineers, built an app for the blind in high school with > 3 million users, and has been [building products](https://www.businessinsider.com/14-year-old-works-11-hours-a-day-at-an-iphone-app-startup-and-concludes-it-was-like-heaven-2013-10) for the last 15 years. He interned at MakeSchool (W12) in 2013 and [Wit.ai](http://Wit.ai) (W14) in 2014 when he was in middle school.\
\
They’ve been best friends since their first day at Cal, and have built dozens of projects between them — tools for researchers to virtual worlds to campus assistants to meme apps. They were roommates and coworkers at Matic Robots in Mountain View, where they helped lead the team. Shalin will never let Kanyes forget that he scored 10 points higher than him on the SAT.

name: rekursiv.ai
long_description:
We're scaling self-improving AI scientist teams to ideate/experiment/discover, generating new knowledge autonomously. Their discoveries reduced ARC-1/2 costs by 10,000× while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy and yielded material advances on combinatorial ML problems.

We believe that AI is bounded not by compute, but ideas. Scaling to millions of sessions of discovery enables leveraging its own discoveries and presents a novel training source capable of ushering a new era of self-reliant foundational models.
one_liner: Scale AI scientists whose own breakthroughs accelerate the next.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
AI research is bottlenecked by humans. Every advance in ML still runs through a small number of researchers who can only devise and test ideas so fast. Experiments take days, most fail, and the field's progress is gated by how quickly a limited pool of experts can iterate.

We think this is the single biggest lever on the future of AI. Our thesis is that AI progress isn't bounded by compute or data, but it's bounded by the rate at which good ideas get devised and tested. Compute keeps scaling, but the human idea-generation loop doesn't. If you could automate the loop itself: hypothesize, experiment, learn, and repeat, then you could compound discoveries far faster than any human team.

We decided to work on it because we've lived the bottleneck. Between us we spent \~30 years doing ML research at Google, DeepMind, and Luma AI. We kept hitting the same wall: the hard part was never running the code, it was the slow, serial process of engineering the training loops to inform what to try next.

When we built a system that could run that loop autonomously, we found we could shorten the gap between having an idea and knowing whether it was a good one. This has allowed us to explore many exciting ideas that we would have otherwise not tried because it was too time-consuming for us. The results convinced us a self-improvement loop now possible, and that we're the ones to build it.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Long-term, we're building autonomous AI scientists and scaling them from one to millions: a fleet running the scientific method in parallel, each discovery accelerating the next.

And this process will start to compound. Each new method our scientists invent makes the next round of research faster and cheaper, a self-improving loop where discovery accelerates discovery. Concretely, that means a world where breakthroughs that would have taken a field a decade happen in months, where the cost of pushing the frontier drops by orders of magnitude, and where a small team can direct the research output of an entire institution. We start with ML research because it's the loop closest to us and the one that speeds up all the others: an AI scientist that improves AI compounds fastest of all.

Hey YC! We're [Josh](https://rekursiv.ai/josh) and [Dan](https://rekursiv.ai/dan), co-founders of [rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai) 🧪.

[rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai) builds fleets of **AI scientists** that do ML research on their own: they come up with ideas, run thousands of experiments in parallel, learn from the results, and accelerate their own discoveries. In a few days of self-directed research, they invented ideas and algorithms that **matched state-of-the-art accuracy on ARC-AGI of frontier LLMs at up to 10,000× lower cost**, and became the first system to hit **100% on Sudoku** with a neural network trained only on input-output pairs.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106821&key=user_uploads/3527564/0444a495-03fa-4f41-9762-ba134521b2f4)

**Why this matters.**

AI research is bottlenecked by humans. Every advance still runs through a small number of researchers who can only devise and test ideas so fast. Compute keeps scaling; the human idea-generation loop doesn't. We believe **AI progress isn't bounded by compute, it's bounded by the rate at which good ideas get tried and tested**. So instead of scaling one model, we built a system that generates and tests ideas on its own.

**It already works.**

In a few days of self-directed research, our AI scientists set a groundbreaking records on hard benchmarks.

* On **ARC-AGI** (easy for humans, hard for AI), our AI scientists matched top frontier LLM models at up to **10,000× lower cost**.
* On **Sudoku**, they achieved 100% accuracy by running hundreds of experiments over a few days, wrote 100k+ lines of their own code, and invented a new inference method (_Hypothesis-Pinning Search_).
* Every gain came from ideas and algorithms **the system invented itself**. It even debugged its own training bugs and abandoned its own ideas that led to dead ends.

Full write-ups: [ARC-AGI](https://rekursiv.ai/blog/pushing-limits-arc-agi/) · [Sudoku](https://rekursiv.ai/blog/100-percent-accuracy-on-sudoku/)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106821&key=user_uploads/3527564/676b13b6-cc1b-4545-8d14-cc7ae1e9b5a5)

**Who we are.**

We're two ML researchers with 21 years of combined experience at **Google DeepMind and Luma AI**. We spent our careers building frontier generative models. Now we're pointing that experience at a harder problem: AI that discovers on its own.

* **Josh Dillon** — Staff Research Scientist at **Google Research & DeepMind for 13 years**, then led foundational-model pre-training at **Luma AI**. Created **TensorFlow Probability** (\~1M downloads/month).
* **Dan Kondratyuk** — First author of **VideoPoet (ICML 2024 Best Paper)**. Co-developed the models powering **Luma's Dream Machine** and led Luma's realtime World Models team. Previously 5 years at **Google Research**.

**What's next.**

We're pointing the system at harder, more varied challenges and building a platform to share results in real time. The bottleneck now is experiment scale: the more experiments we run, the more discoveries the our AI teams can make. We plan to scale from a few AI scientists to millions, each discovery accelerating the next, until the rate of scientific progress is no longer limited by the number of human researchers.

**Asks.**

* **Got a hard problem or benchmark?** If you have a benchmark or research problem you'd love an autonomous team of scientists to attack, we want to hear it. Email [contact@rekursiv.ai](mailto:contact@rekursiv.ai).
* **Researchers & engineers:** We're hiring **Founding Scientists** and **Engineers** (Bay Area or remote). If you love running thousands of experiments and figuring out what the results mean, reach out at [hiring@rekursiv.ai](mailto:hiring@rekursiv.ai)
* **Just want to nerd out about autonomous science?** Drop us a line, always happy to chat.

— Josh & Dan, [rekursiv.ai](http://rekursiv.ai)

question_answers.answer:
The three of us met building Garry's List. Every time we moved between AI tools we pasted the same API keys into the next one and explained the work all over again. 

No existing tools were built for a team, either. We wanted one thing all three of us could prompt together, which is why gbrain.io is multiplayer.

Initially, building this meant the three of us in a room spinning up an agent harness, initializing memory; installing skills, manually setting up integrations to external tools, and pasting API keys in one at a time. 

After copy-pasting that setup for a bunch of our friends, we built [gbrain.io](http://gbrain.io) for the world: the same thing, in the cloud, that sets itself up in one click.

launches.tagline: The shared learning layer for agents.
launches.body:
Hey everyone! I'm Nikos, the founder of Glen.

**TL;DR**

Glen is building the organizational learning and context layer for agents.

Every agent session your team runs produces reasoning worth keeping, and nearly all of it is discarded the moment the window closes.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T0CkjYfo3k3FB40_R7UPNfONO-SdgfKB](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T0CkjYfo3k3FB40_R7UPNfONO-SdgfKB/view?usp=sharing)

Glen is the layer that unifies every agent and model your company run. Glen pulls in agent sessions from Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, plus Slack messages, GitHub prs, tickets, docs and calls. When a new agent picks up a task, Glen finds relevant prior context and injects it in the agents context window to steer it, producing knowledge work that is significantly higher quality, faster and cheaper than ever before.

And Glen does more. It unifies all of your org's context: query the original agent behind any line of code, search every session your org has ever run, dynamic skill distillation, multiplayer agents, unified transcripts you can hand between Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor mid-task, and a company brain in Slack.\
\
Composio scaled usage from 2 users to org wide. Over a dozen SF startups use Glen. I’m onboarding new teams every week, email me at [nikos@tryglen.com](mailto:nikos@tryglen.com) to get set up with early access.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111187&key=user_uploads/3237090/2d8c514f-6318-491a-937e-87f1d3e32ae6)

**What Glen does practically**

* Relevant context injected on every prompt which steers your model to do knowledge work more efficiently saving your time, money and headaches. These injections can consist or niche knowledge unique to the repo you are working in, high level understanding of relevant sub systems, and previous approaches teammates took to similar problems. Glen surfaces the prior work that matters automatically, so tasks finish faster and cost fewer tokens with no loss in quality, because what lands in the window is the relevant work rather than more of it. You can lazy-prompt instead of retyping the same background every session. So far, internal evals show about a **29% reduction in token spend** and **21% reduction in task completion time**.

  \
  **Also…**
* PR review with the original context. Highlight any code in a diff and ask why it's there. Glen queries the agent session that produced it and answers from the actual trace instead of guessing from the diff.
* Code search across every agent trace. Ask your coding agent anything about the codebase and it searches every session any agent in your org has run, so the answer comes from the work that produced the code.
* A skill library the whole org shares. Glen distills what your team does into skills, publishes them where everyone can use them, and surfaces the right one automatically when someone hits a task it covers.
* Multiplayer agents. You and your designer work the same deck in parallel, you on copy and them on design. Make a design edit and your agent applies the style theirs has learned. When they touch the copy, their agent writes in the voice yours was taught. Neither of you hands anything off.
* No lock-in to a model provider. Transcripts from Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor all land in one place, and you can hand a session from one to another mid-task, with Glen converting the format so the next agent picks up exactly where the last one stopped. Your context, your skills, and your shared artifacts come with you, so moving between providers costs nothing.
* We have a Slackbot company brain too!

**Deployed org-wide at Composio**. Composio was my first design partner. It started with two users, grew to about twenty naturally as I iterated on the product, and is now used across the company. Also in use at over a dozen other companies!

In the last 30 days alone, Glen injected **10s of millions of** characters of organizational context into their agents. These injections steer the models used by these teams, giving them a competative edge that allows them to perform knowledge work better, faster, and cheaper.

**My Ask**

If you are at a startup and are reading this, there's a 80% chance Glen would be a great addition to your productivity stack. Most teams run agents heavily, and if yours is tired of re-explaining meetings, Slack, tickets, conventions, and what past sessions already worked out, that's exactly what Glen removes. \
\
I'd love to chat, and I'll come to your office, or wherever you are, and set you up for a with a early access workspace before public availability. Just shoot me an email at [nikos@tryglen.com](mailto:nikos@tryglen.com)!

launches.tagline: Record how you work and turn that into agents
launches.body:
screenpipe records what you do, see and hear on your computer, makes it searchable, and gives agents the context to understand how you actually work. The project has 20K+ GitHub stars.

<https://youtu.be/c1jV6E9pyug>

Most AI agents start every task with partial context.

They can read the prompt and apps you connect. They do not remember the meeting where a decision was made, the tab you opened last Tuesday, the exact steps you took to fix a problem, or the edge case you discovered while doing the work.

screenpipe runs quietly in the background and captures screen and audio context on your machine. Then you can ask:

* maintain a second brain for every person, projects, tasks, meetings


* turn the workday into a daily recap and time breakdown for standups or client billing
* maintain a personal CRM from the people, conversations, and follow-ups seen during the day
* find commitments mentioned in meetings or messages that never made it into a task list
* analyze repeated work and produce a list of workflows worth automating
* save prompts and context from Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT into a searchable journal

Agents can use screenpipe as long-term memory, so they work from what actually happened instead of only what you remembered to paste into a prompt.

The same foundation also works across team machines. Teams can map repeated workflows, generate SOPs, find bottlenecks, and identify automation opportunities across the tools where work actually happens.

screenpipe is open source and local-first. You control what gets recorded, can exclude apps, windows, and URLs, and choose where your data lives.

I’ve been building my own AI second brain since 2020, but it could only remember what I explicitly saved. I built screenpipe so my AI could understand what I was actually doing across my screen and conversations. Other people began using it for the same reason. Today, we’re turning that foundation into context for personal and team agents.

**Our ask**

Try screenpipe and comment with the agent you would build if it could remember everything you’ve worked on.

Try screenpipe: <https://screenpipe.com>
